summary: The Budgeting for a Better America Act modifies the federal budget and appropriations process by moving the United States Congress from an annual budget cycle to a biennial (two-year) budget cycle. It also establishes the National Commission on Fiscal Responsibility and Reform to propose fiscal sustainability recommendations with expedited legislative consideration, requires long-term unfunded obligation analyses in the President's budget, mandates annual supplemental budget submissions, requires joint hearings on the fiscal state of the nation, and adds budgetary training to new member orientations.

affected_groups.effect: Members must participate in biennial budgeting, attend new member orientation budget briefings, serve on or interact with new commission structures, and participate in expedited voting procedures for fiscal recommendations.

The President must include long-term unfunded obligation analyses in the budget and submit annual supplemental administrative budgets; federal agencies must provide requested information to the Fiscal Responsibility and Reform Commission.
affected_groups.group: The President and Executive Branch Agencies

key_provisions: Revises the congressional budget timetable to establish biennial concurrent budget resolutions covering two consecutive fiscal years beginning in even-numbered years.

Establishes an 18-member National Commission on Fiscal Responsibility and Reform tasked with recommending policies for medium-term and long-term fiscal sustainability, aiming for a 3 percent deficit-to-GDP ratio within 10 years.
Provides expedited legislative consideration and special joint resolution procedures in both the House and Senate for recommendations approved by the Commission.
Requires the President's annual budget submission to include an analysis of long-term unfunded obligations in entitlement programs over 25-, 50-, and 75-year windows.
Requires the President to submit an annual supplemental administrative budget starting December 1, 2028.
Mandates that the chairs of the House and Senate Budget Committees and the Comptroller General conduct an annual joint hearing reviewing the federal government's audited financial statements.
Requires the Congressional Budget Office to provide a budgetary briefing during official orientation training for newly elected members of Congress before they are sworn in.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or appropriations authorized for the operation of the National Commission on Fiscal Responsibility and Reform.
Details on how existing multi-year federal contracts or ongoing annual programs will transition fully into the new biennial timelines.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Budgeting for a Better America Act modifies the federal budget and appropriations process by moving the United States Congress from an annual budget cycle to a biennial (two-year) budget cycle. It also establishes the National Commission on Fiscal Responsibility and Reform to propose fiscal sustainability recommendations with expedited legislative consideration, requires long-term unfunded obligation analyses in the President's budget, mandates annual supplemental budget submissions, requires joint hearings on the fiscal state of the nation, and adds budgetary training to new member orientations.
summary_detail.significance: This bill changes how the federal government plans and executes its budget by shifting to a two-year cycle and creates a high-profile commission with fast-track legislative powers to tackle long-term deficits and entitlement spending. Because the text explicitly focuses on procedural rules and structural commissions rather than immediate spending caps or program cuts, its potential significance is rated as moderate.
